GlobalLogic explains the reusable design behind Haystack’s hospital robot

A new engineering interview describes a modular mobile base and a caregiver-following mode for complex hospital environments.

The Robot Report ↗4 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 2

New details about an existing project

A November 4 interview in The Robot Report describes GlobalLogic’s engineering work with Haystack Robotics, begun during the pandemic. The aim was more consistent UV disinfection with less manual effort. This is new reporting on the design, not a new robot launch or a new disinfection-efficacy trial.

A reusable mobile architecture

The team separated the mobile base from its UV payload so other equipment could be mounted later. The architecture combines perception, onboard processing and ROS-based programming and sensor fusion. Engineers said motor-control approaches and software components have already informed other projects.

Caregivers remain part of the workflow

Alongside autonomous navigation, a following mode lets a caregiver open doors and prepare rooms. Cost, return on investment, medical standards and staff acceptance remain barriers. Crowded corridors and urgent tasks require workflow changes; the report does not establish that robots can immediately replace staff across hospital duties.
